name: Primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disease
aliases: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of large atypical CD30+ T-cells in skin biopsy
Solitary or localized nodules or tumors on the skin without extracutaneous disease at diagnosis
Immunohistochemical confirmation of CD30 expression in >75% of tumor cells
No evidence of systemic lymphoma by imaging and bone marrow biopsy
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating clonality supportive but not mandatory

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of CD30+ large atypical T-cells in skin biopsy with compatible clinical presentation and exclusion of systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary correlation including dermatology, pathology, and oncology.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or localized erythematous to violaceous nodules or tumors
searchTerms: single red or purple skin lumps

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histological presence of large atypical CD30+ T-cells in skin lesions
searchTerms: specific immune cell presence in skin

common.symptomName: Ulceration of cutaneous nodules or tumors
Indolent course with slow lesion progression

occasional.symptomName: Multiple skin lesions appearing over time
Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

occasional.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of ulcerated lesions
Localized pain or tenderness at lesion site

searchTerms: spread to lymph nodes or lungs

rare.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (weight loss, night sweats)
searchTerms: systemic symptoms like chills and weight loss
B symptoms including sweating and fever
skin lesions that disappear on their own

laboratory: Immunohistochemistry showing CD30 positivity in >75% of atypical T-cells
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating clonality
imaging: PET-CT or CT scan to exclude extracutaneous involvement
other: Skin biopsy histopathology showing large anaplastic lymphoid cells

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows CD30+ cells but with polymorphous infiltrate

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)
Evidence of extracutaneous dissemination on imaging
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.

Bekkenk MW, Geelen FA, van Voorst Vader PC, et al. Primary and secondary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorders: a report from the Dutch Cutaneous Lymphoma Group on the long-term follow-up data of 219 patients and guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. Blood. 2000;95(12):3653-3661.
Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al., editors. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
